coverageNote: Enumerated 6 units and 35 files from disk, matching the expected counts exactly. Units: the domain root (04-opportunities-casting, holding opportunities-casting-index.md, opportunities-casting-cx.md, 04.06-band-member-wanted.md, 04.07-open-calls-festival-showcase-competition.md) plus the five sub-domain directories 04.01-04.05. Every file was read in full through the 3a/3b/3c cycle. Dimension 4 (Constraint Explicitness) and dimension 5 (Success Measurability) are marked N/A on every unit: project constraint axes (budget, timeline, team, compliance) and success metrics are owned by meta/constraints.md and the vision layer, which are outside this domain; where this domain does state operational numbers (04.02.04 tier latencies, 04.05.03 handoff bounds, 04.01.03 facet bounds) they are numeric and testable, so scoring them here would only flatter the result. Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) is applicable only to the domain root (Sonicbids/ReverbNation/JoinMyBand/Bandmix/Craigslist named with a specific capability gap) and to 04.02 (04.02.01 DT-03's rot analysis of the same incumbents); N/A on 04.01, 04.03, 04.04, 04.05, which are mechanism units with no positioning role. A large number of `[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` markers survive across the tree pointing at a stage that the files themselves record as having run and closed; only those markers that carry no owner AND are not covered by a properly-tracked open question elsewhere are reported (04.01.02 blocked-invitee, 04.02.03 setlist re-score, 04.06 band dissolution, the five slots in 04.03's CX). Markers whose substance is answered downstream were followed and dropped, including 04.07's deadline-timezone row (answered by 04.01.01 D-10 + 04.03.01 line 87: deadlines are absolute instants), 04.01's CX-01 admin-override slot (resolved by 04.01.03 D-10), 04.04's CX-01 shortlist-notification and un-rejection slots (resolved by 04.04.02 Q-02 and 04.04.03 line 178), 04.04's CX-02 permission slot (resolved in full by 04.04.03's three-grants table), 04.02's CX-05 permission slot (resolved by 04.02.04 D-14) and 04.05's CX-04 permission slot (resolved by 04.05.02 + 04.05.04 D-07).

findings.claim: Member-wanted posts are simultaneously required to carry a decide-by derived from an 'event date' and declared to have no date at all, and a third file gives them a fourth lifecycle rule. Nothing defines what a member-wanted ad's event date is, so an implementer must invent either a required date field on the most common amateur post or a default duration.
findings.evidence: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:101 taxonomy row: "| Member wanted | 06 | Venue-local wall-clock | Derived — the event date | **Yes** (presence outcome) | Performance | Mutual selection, outcome is Band membership — see 04.06 |". 04.01.01:321 D-16: "**presence types** (dep/sub call, function/private hire, audition/casting call, crew, camp, support slot, **member wanted**, open-mic — every type whose date is venue-local wall-clock) derive it from the **event date** … It is **always present** … **The decide-by is what closes the post**", and 04.01.01:110 "**no type can publish without a decide-by**". Against this, 04.06-band-member-wanted.md:36 Behavior table: "| Lifecycle | Deadline-bound | **Open-ended; runs for months** |" and 04.06:63 States: "| Open | Ad posted | Live, open-ended, **no deadline** |". A third, different rule appears at 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:60: "| Member wanted (04.06) | Recency, 90-day half-life | Poster closes it, **or 90 days elapse** | 14 days |". No file states what event a member-wanted ad's date refers to.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent the member-wanted post's date semantics: require an event date the type has no concept of (contradicting 04.06's open-ended shape), synthesise a decide-by from the 90-day board half-life (a board-side presentation rule that 04.02.01 D-06 explicitly says is 'presentation only … never a lifecycle transition'), or exempt the type from D-16 (contradicting 'no type can publish without a decide-by'). Each choice changes when the post auto-closes, when 04.04.01's `dormant` trigger fires, and what ceiling bounds every hold's resolve-by.

findings.claim: 04.01.01 D-16 says the decide-by on briefs and open calls is an asked field pre-filled with, and defaulting to, the submission deadline; 04.07 D-05 ratifies the opposite — that it is not derived from the deadline — on the explicit ground that a deadline-valued decide-by is a lie told to 2,000 applicants. Both cannot hold, and the difference decides whether the field is a required non-defaulted input.
findings.evidence: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:96 "| Brief / RFP | 05, 10 | Absolute deadline | **Asked** — a real field, **pre-filled with the deadline** | …" and :98 "| Festival / showcase / competition open call | … | **Asked** — a real field, **pre-filled with the deadline** (04.07 D-05) | …", reinforced at :109-111 "The two `Asked` rows … **Both still default to the deadline if left alone**, which is why **no type can publish without a decide-by** either way." Against this, 04.07-open-calls-festival-showcase-competition.md:105 D-05: "**The decide-by is a real, asked field on this type**, not derived from the deadline … Deriving it would tell 2,000 acts they will hear by 1 March, **which is the ghosting D-04 exists to prevent**, generated by the platform rather than the Operator", and 04.07:44 "So this type carries a decide-by **the Operator states**".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide whether an open call can publish with an untouched, deadline-valued decide-by. Under 04.01.01 it can (and the applicant is then told 'decisions by 1 March' — the exact harm 04.07 D-04/D-05 exist to prevent); under 04.07 D-05 it cannot and the field must be blocking-required with no default. This also determines what 04.04.01 D-05's hold ceiling and 04.07's waitlist resolve-by are bounded by.

findings.claim: The 25-slot limit is stated twice as a 'soft ceiling' and once as an unconditional refusal, in a file that elsewhere distinguishes warn-from-block explicitly. Two implementers build different controls.
findings.evidence: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:47 "**Soft ceiling: 25 slots per post** — past that it is a hiring round, and the shape that serves it is the open call (04.07)"; :313 D-08 "…the post's status follows its slots. **Soft ceiling 25 slots**". Against this, :185 edge case "| Post needs 30 slots (a festival's whole crew) | **Refused above 25**; routed to the open call shape (04.07) … | \"That's a hiring round, not an opportunity — open calls handle 30 slots properly.\" |". The same file draws the distinction deliberately elsewhere — :196 tier-2 duplicate detection is "**warn, never block**" and :318 D-13 repeats "a false block is worse than a duplicate … hence warn-not-block" — so 'soft' is load-bearing vocabulary here, not loose prose.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a 26-slot post is blocked at publish or warned and allowed.

findings.claim: The board's type-scoped behaviour table claims to enumerate the 04.01.01 taxonomy but covers 10 of its 12 types, leaving `Open-mic / showcase slot` and `General call` with no primary sort, no board-exit rule, no tombstone window and no freshness interval.
findings.evidence: 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:46 "Types from the 04.01.01 taxonomy. \"Primary sort\" is the tiebreaker *within* fit, never a replacement for it." — the table at :49-60 lists Dep/sub, Session, Function, Audition, Brief/RFP, Crew, Open call, Camp, Support slot, Member wanted. 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:90-103 defines twelve types, adding "| **Open-mic / showcase slot** | 08, 09 | Venue-local wall-clock | …" and "| **General call** | — | **Poster picks; both offered** | Derived — follows whichever semantics the poster picked | …". The freshness rule at 04.02.01:62 has the same hole: "48 h for dep/session/function/crew/support, 30 days for member-wanted, never for deadline-bearing types". 04.02.01:254 D-05 makes this normative: "Board decay, sort and tombstone windows are **type-scoped**".
findings.forcedInvention: The sort key, board-exit condition, tombstone retention and freshness interval for open-mic slots and for `General call`. `General call` is the harder one: its date semantics are poster-chosen (04.01.01:103), so it cannot even be classified as deadline-bearing or not without a rule.

findings.claim: The behaviour when a setlist changes after material scoring has run is left as two bare `[PENDING]` markers pointing at a stage the tree records as completed, with no owner, and is not covered by any of the file's four open questions — yet the material ranking it invalidates is the urgent-fill cascade's order.
findings.evidence: 04.02.03-material-aware-dep-matching.md:52 "| Setlist changes after matching | Score invalidated. Setlists change constantly, often on the day. | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — **re-score, or accept staleness?** |" and :64 "| Stale | Setlist changed post-scoring | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |". The same file records that stage as run and closed at :99: "Re-pointed from the **completed** `/ideate-discover` Step 5." Its Q-01 to Q-04 (:97-100) cover the beachhead, arrangement versions, repertoire ubiquity and private credits — none covers re-scoring. The stake is set at :44 "Cascade fires in confidence order (04.04.04)" and 04.04.04-urgent-fill-first-accept-cascade.md:39 "Cascade order resolves: the poster's ranked list, **refined by material confidence**", while 04.01.02-targeting-distribution-controls.md:52 fixes already-invited positions as immutable.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a mid-cascade setlist edit re-scores and re-orders the un-reached tail of the cascade, or the pool is frozen at its original scoring.

findings.claim: What happens when a poster invites someone who has blocked them is a bare `[PENDING]` with no owner, pointing at a stage the same file records as completed, and it is not covered by any of that file's three open questions — while another file defers to it as though it were a tracked question.
findings.evidence: 04.01.02-targeting-distribution-controls.md:49 "| Poster targets someone who has blocked them | **Invite silently fails — but silently to *whom*?** Telling the poster leaks the block. | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — a Trust & Safety (24) boundary. |". The same file's Q-02 records the stage as finished: ":101 Re-pointed from `/ideate-discover` Step 5, **which has run and left this open**"; its Q-01, Q-02 and Q-03 (:100-102) cover invite-vs-eligibility, confidentiality and the trusted-network cold start — none covers blocks. 04.02.01-opportunity-board-search.md:174 then defers to it as if tracked: "Whether the *poster* is told their invite failed is **04.01.02's open question** (leaking a block)". The adjacent row at 04.01.02:54 does define the analogous case ("Invited person deletes their account / is suspended … cascade advances to the next name … No leak of *why* they dropped"), which makes the omission of the block case a decision withheld rather than an oversight covered by a general rule.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a blocked-by invitee is silently skipped with the cascade advancing (as for a suspended invitee), or the poster is told the invite failed, and what the poster sees in either case.

findings.claim: The orphaned-post case when a band dissolves mid-search is a bare `[PENDING]` with no owner pointing at a completed stage; the properly-tracked question elsewhere covers only who inherits the disposition debt, not what happens to the live post.
findings.evidence: 04.06-band-member-wanted.md:56 "| Band splits up mid-search | **Post orphaned; the entity that posted no longer coheres** | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |". The same file records that stage as finished at :103: "Re-pointed from `/ideate-discover` Step 5, **which has run** and left 04.01.02 Q-02 open." Its Q-01 to Q-04 cover mutual selection, the unpaid-rehearsal line, splits and confidentiality — none covers dissolution. The nearest tracked question is scoped to the debt only: 04.04.01-review-queue-triage.md:228 Q-05 "**Who inherits the obligation when the posting org dissolves mid-queue?** … this feature can **detect** the state but cannot **assign the debt**", echoed at 04.05.01-disposition-close-out-obligation.md:259 Q-05. The post's own lifecycle has no matching trigger: 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:246 enumerates "| Withdrawn | Poster cancels, or source context cancelled, or poster suspended |" with no dissolution case.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a post whose acting identity has dissolved stays live and keeps accepting submissions (accruing further obligations nobody can discharge), auto-withdraws, or holds in a new state.

findings.claim: The audition-waiver rule is normative but untestable as written — 'strong evidence' with no threshold dimension anywhere — and the question that would have defined it is marked RESOLVED as 'a poster-set threshold' without saying a threshold over what.
findings.evidence: 04.03.03-audition-tasks-media-submission.md:102 D-03: "**Strong evidence** should **waive** the audition (CX-05)"; :59 edge case "| Applicant has strong verified evidence for exactly this | Task should be waived or reduced (CX-05) … | \"Sam's played this set twice — skip the audition?\" |"; :76 state "| Waived | **Evidence threshold met** (CX-05) | \"No audition needed — your credits cover it\" |". Q-03 is closed on the strength of one CX line — :111 "✅ **RESOLVED — a poster-set threshold.** … CX-05, synthesis answer 2: *\"Evidence resolved → **threshold met** → audition waived or reduced. **Poster-set thresholds**, since the judgement is theirs.\"*" — and 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:153 carries exactly that sentence and nothing more. The evidence model it would be a threshold over is purely ordinal: 04.03.02-evidence-backed-application.md:38-46 ranks five evidence types "in descending order of strength" with no counts, scores or cut-offs. By contrast the same sub-tree specifies an equivalent bar numerically where it has decided one — 04.02.04-alert-subscriptions-delivery.md:52 "material confidence ≥ \"played this exact set\" or \"played ≥60% of these songs in the last 24 months\"".
findings.forcedInvention: The quantity the poster's waiver threshold is set over (count of attested credits, evidence tier, material-confidence percentage, prior collaboration with the poster), and therefore what the poster is asked for at task-definition time and what the applicant is shown before spending the time (which D-02 requires).

findings.claim: Handoff mode is fixed by a target reference that must exist at post time, but cold-typing is guaranteed complete for every type, and the per-type table assigns dep/sub, support-slot and crew wins to join mode with no create-mode fallback — so the handoff for a cold-typed dep win is unspecified.
findings.evidence: 04.05.03-won-opportunity-handoff.md:43 "**The mode is determined by whether the opportunity carries a target reference, and that reference must exist at post time — never at win time.**" and :39 "| **Create** | A downstream entity that did not exist comes into being | The opportunity has **no target reference** — a function gig, a standalone brief |". The per-type table at :52 then assigns "| Dep / sub call | A **substitution** on an existing show's lineup + a gig on the winner's calendar | **Join** | 17, 18 | Names who came **off** (DT-04) |" with no fallback, while the session row at :53 shows the authors adding one where they thought of it: "| Session call | A contributor on a project | **Join (or Create if no project exists)** | 07 |". Cold-typing is guaranteed for every type by 04.01.01-opportunity-post-type-taxonomy.md:307 D-02: "**Cold-typing remains complete** — this feature does not require 17/18 to launch", and 04.01.01:145 Happy Path B is the cold path. The tracked question covers only field placement, not this behaviour: 04.05.03:260 Q-07 "**The requirement itself is not open** — D-12 fixes it … only **where the two fields land on the Opportunity data model**".
findings.forcedInvention: What a cold-typed dep-call or support-slot win hands off to. Create mode is incoherent for a substitution (there is no lineup to substitute into and nothing states that a show is created), and the no-target degradation at D-08 ("the agreed terms in writing + an importable calendar entry") is written for the case where the whole target *domain* is absent, not for a post that simply carries no target.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX file leaves five of its twenty-five synthesis slots as bare `[PENDING]` markers with no owner, all pointing at a stage the sub-domain's own files record as run and closed — including both remaining slots of CX-05, the cross-cut that carries the audition-waiver rule.
findings.evidence: 04.03-submission-audition-cx.md:103 (CX-03, permission intersection) "3. **Permission intersection**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`"; :105 (CX-03, state transition) "5. **State transition conflict**: `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`"; :154, :155 and :156 (CX-05, permission intersection / notification fan-out / state transition conflict) each "`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`". None carries an owner or a live deferral target, and the stage is recorded as finished throughout the sub-domain — 04.03.04-blind-review-mode.md:66 "Re-pointed from the **completed** `/ideate-discover` Step 5", 04.03.05-outbound-pitch-unsolicited.md:47 "Re-pointed from the **completed** `/ideate-discover` Step 5." CX-05 is also the cross-cut the sub-domain leans on for the waiver rule (04.03.03 Q-03 closes against CX-05's synthesis answer 2), so three of its five slots being unanswered leaves that rule with no permission, notification or state-change semantics.
findings.forcedInvention: Nothing is directly invented from the markers themselves; the defect is that the sub-domain's declared open work is untracked — no owner, and a deferral target that has already run and closed, so no later stage will pick them up.
